findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:253 pins the proposal-side comparand to the literal status:'open' while comparing it against the live finding.status read at line 242. Because lattice finding_resolve (packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:827) mutates f.status = 'resolved' in place without re-deriving the managed comparison, exactEvidenceMatches flips to false the moment an imported managed finding is resolved. That drives semanticDigestValid false in verifyManagedReviewEvidence, which returns code 'managed_receipt_invalid' at packages/main/src/core/review-run.ts:1551. 'managed_receipt_invalid' is NOT a member of SUPERSEDED_PASS_ISSUE_CODES (packages/main/src/core/review-run.ts:130-139), so the issue survives the supersede filter at line 1697 and lands in evidenceState.invalid, which hard-blocks REVIEW->TEST at packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:790 before the blocking-severity check at line 855 is ever evaluated. The deadlock is structural: isFindingBlocking (packages/main/src/core/advisory.ts:57) requires status === 'open', so resolving the finding is the only workflow-sanctioned way to clear it, yet resolving is precisely what invalidates its receipt. Contributing factor: the managed finding signature (signFinding version 4, packages/main/src/core/finding-verify.ts:74-89) omits category/evidenceState/uncertaintyReason/files, whereas the native path (version 6, lines 53-72) binds them via nativeFindingSemantics, so the managed path depends entirely on this over-strict runtime comparison for those fields. No test in packages/main/src/tasks/managed-review-evidence-smoke.ts exercises resolve-after-import, so the gap is uncovered.
